dct_creator_sm: Government of the Northwest Territories, Environment and Climate Change.
dct_description_sm:
The Coppermine river watershed have been identified as one of the most important and pristine river systems in the Canadian Central Arctic. Development pressures within the watershed currently include diamond mining and ongoing base metal exploration, as well as winter and all season road development, and recreational use. Potential cumulative effects of these developments require ongoing monitoring and assessment of the watershed’s water chemistry and water quantity. Both Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) and the Department of Environment and Climate Change, GNWT has been collecting water chemistry and quantity (flow) data within this watershed since 1960. Monitoring has increased both spatially and seasonally since the first diamond mine (Ekati) opened within this basin. This dataset includes water quality monitoring data collected since 2000.  Since 2000, water quality data has been collected at 11 sites throughout the basin.  However, since 2010 only 5 sites remain active, all within the upper basin in the NWT. Water quality analysis is carried out for routine parameters including: physicals, solids, nutrients, ions, metals (including mercury), and chlorophyl A. Status and Trend reporting and monitoring program evaluation has been carried out approximate every 5 years.
